insight.title: Why Doing Something Good Makes You Act Worse
insight.subtitle: Why a healthy lunch or a productive morning often leads to bad decisions later

sections.text: You finish a difficult workout or clear your inbox early. Feeling virtuous, you later find yourself justifying a distraction, a snack, or a purchase you would usually avoid.
This is "moral licensing." When we do something we consider "good," it gives us a subconscious hall pass to be "bad." We feel we’ve earned the right to take a shortcut.
This pattern keeps us stuck in a cycle of one step forward, one step back. We use our discipline in one area to justify a lack of focus in another.
Try this today: The next time you feel proud of a small accomplishment today, skip the immediate reward.
Your best choices shouldn't be used as currency to buy your worst ones.
